automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.rule: Public sources must display an unambiguous publication or update date within the prior 48 hours. Date-only sources at the lower boundary are excluded.

federation.collector_boundary: Keep only local AI-assisted-development practice implications; do not create local entity coverage.

qualifying_updates.title: Open source license compliance generally available
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub made enterprise license-policy checks generally available. A ruleset can require license-compliance results before merging dependency changes; noncompliant dependencies require removal or replacement, a policy amendment, or a package exception. Policy changes emit audit events, and an API endpoint can check whether a package complies with policy.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: When an agent proposes a package change, run dependency and license policy checks before merge, preserve the exception or approval evidence, and keep package selection separate from a model's recommendation. Agent-accessible policy queries can prevent a known-ineligible suggestion, but do not replace review of provenance, security, or fit.
qualifying_updates.follow_up: Route to normal raw ingest only if a maintainer wants a durable AI-assisted dependency-selection and license-exception control; keep GitHub feature coverage upstream.

qualifying_updates.title: Cloud Agent Canvases and Environment Improvements
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Cursor reports that cloud agents can create interactive canvases that teams share by link. Its Environments API is in beta for programmatically creating and managing cloud environments, which can now include up to 300 repositories.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Treat a programmatically created agent environment as a governed runtime: declare repository membership, initialization, credentials, network and cleanup policy, then retain those settings with the resulting review artifact. A shareable canvas is a handoff surface that still needs content review and access control before distribution.
qualifying_updates.follow_up: Route to normal raw ingest only if a maintainer wants a local environment-control-plane and artifact-sharing checklist; keep Cursor product details upstream.

qualifying_updates.title: How do you prove your AI governance works? Lessons from Toronto
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The Agentic AI Foundation describes practitioner examples in which tool availability is filtered by application purpose, access checks occur at the service boundary, and governance evidence connects identity, permissions, authorization, execution, and verified outcomes. It also warns that MCP-only controls do not govern equivalent actions through scripts or browser automation.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: A governed tool-call workflow should prove which user or agent had which tools and permissions, where enforcement occurred, what was approved, and the resulting outcome. Test controls across every reachable action path, including shell and browser routes, rather than treating an MCP audit entry or successful response as proof of authorization or completion.
qualifying_updates.follow_up: Route to normal raw ingest only if a maintainer wants a durable governance-evidence checklist spanning MCP, scripts, browsers, and other action paths.

qualifying_updates.title: Stack Overflow for Agents triples signups with ChatGPT plugin
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: OpenAI reports that Stack Overflow for Agents is organizing information from systems such as Slack and Google Docs into verified knowledge for people and agents. The customer describes giving coding agents a development environment and a plan, then expanding its product from intake toward sharing knowledge gained in individual sessions across the organization.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Use an explicit plan and a bounded development environment as the starting context for coding-agent work. Treat a knowledge base as a lifecycle: source intake, verification, controlled agent access, and durable sharing of validated learning are separate responsibilities; a customer story is adoption evidence, not a universal productivity benchmark.
qualifying_updates.follow_up: Route to normal raw ingest only if a maintainer wants a source-backed plan-plus-environment and verified-knowledge-lifecycle pattern; do not generalize the reported customer outcomes.

search_notes: Searched public primary vendor changelogs, foundation practice publications, and direct official links surfaced by secondary leads for context, agent workflows, code review, MCP governance, environment control, licensing, and adoption topics.
No private, proprietary, sensitive, PII, or company-internal repository content was sent to external services.
Every qualifying item has a visible October 16, 2026 date and is within the strict 48-hour window.
follow_up_notes: Collector remains raw-only: do not update docs/wiki or move this artifact to raw/processed in this run.
If ingesting the license-compliance item, retain policy, exception, audit-event, and independent package-review boundaries.
If ingesting the environment and canvas item, distinguish environment configuration, access control, and content review from the vendor product facts.
If ingesting the governance article, retain the distinction between an attempted or successful tool call and proof of authorization and verified outcome across all action paths.
If ingesting the customer story, qualify it as an attributed adoption example rather than a transferable delivery metric.
